title: Pipeline state paths — the transient/durable partition under _bmad-output/
description: THE single classification of every top-level entry the shipped machinery constructs under the pipeline output directory. Each entry is TRANSIENT (per-run coordination state, never tracked) or DURABLE (a pipeline artifact the consumer commits). install.sh renders the transient half into the consumer's .gitignore as a marked block, uninstall.sh removes that block, and invariant I95 in scripts/validate-enforcement-map.sh binds this file to the machinery in BOTH directions -- a declared entry whose producer does not construct it fails the push, and a path the machinery constructs that is declared nowhere fails it too. Written because the distribution shipped NO ignore rule at all: install.sh had zero references to .gitignore, and the reference consumer had hand-added four transient paths to its own .gitignore over roughly four hundred releases while three others -- .wait-beats/ (134 files), .driver/ (3) and .context-sensor-state (1) -- silently became tracked. The partition, not just the transient list, is the mechanism: a NEW state path fails the push until it is classified, so the ignore block cannot fall behind the machinery the way a hand-written list did. A blanket _bmad-output/.* glob was measured and REJECTED -- the reference consumer tracks _bmad-output/.audit-accepted-exceptions, a deliberate committed file the distribution has zero knowledge of, and a shipped glob would silently untrack consumer-owned dot-entries that no declaration here can enumerate.

block_begin.description: First line of the managed .gitignore block. install.sh deletes from this marker to block_end before appending a fresh block, which is what makes a reinstall idempotent rather than additive. It is matched as a literal whole line, so a consumer that indents or reflows it gets a SECOND block rather than a silently skipped update -- the visible failure, deliberately.

block_end.description: Last line of the managed block. Present so the deletion is bounded: without a terminator, a marker-to-EOF cut would take every rule a consumer wrote after installing.

root.description: The pipeline output directory, prefixed onto each transient entry's ignore pattern. Declared rather than hard-coded in install.sh so the rendered block and the invariant's grammar cannot disagree about where these paths live.

paths.description: Every top-level name the shipped machinery constructs under root, partitioned. Derived from a grep over core/hooks/, core/scripts/, core/session-driver/ and core/git-hooks/ for occurrences of ${STATE_DIR}/, ${LOG_DIR}/ or a literal _bmad-output/ on a non-comment line; I95 re-derives that same population and set-compares it against this array, so the two cannot drift.

name.description: The top-level component under root, exactly as the derivation grammar yields it -- no trailing slash and no glob suffix, because this string is the JOIN KEY against that grammar's output and any decoration would make the set-compare fail on a correctly declared path.

transient.description: true when the path is per-run coordination state that must never be committed. The transient half is what renders into .gitignore. Classification was validated against the reference consumer: every durable entry is tracked there, and every transient entry is untracked EXCEPT the three that are this release's subject.

producer.description: A shipped file that constructs this path on a non-comment line. I95 checks it with the same grammar that derived the population, so a producer naming a file that merely mentions the path in prose does not satisfy it. Where several files construct a path, this names one -- the check is that the declaration points at real machinery, not that it enumerates every caller.

ignore.description: The .gitignore pattern rendered for a transient entry, root prefix included. Required on every transient entry and forbidden on a durable one; I95 enforces both directions. It is a separate field from name because a directory needs a trailing slash and the mktemp fallback needs a suffix glob, and putting either into name would break the join.

reason.description: What writes this path and why it is on the side of the partition it is on. Required because a classification nobody can audit is the hand-written list this file replaces.

block_begin: # BEGIN AI/DLC transient pipeline state (managed by install.sh -- do not edit)

paths.name: .adversarial-stop
paths.reason: Marker the continuation hook writes to stop an adversarial review cycle. Meaningful only within the run that wrote it.

paths.name: .audit-watermark
paths.reason: Genesis commit recorded for --audit range selection. Local to the machine running the audit; a committed watermark would impose one checkout's history on every other.

paths.name: .ai-dlc-context-nonce
paths.reason: The append-only set of context-provenance nonces for this checkout. Transient for a reason stronger than tidiness: the whole property the marker buys is that the nonce reaches the lead only through a hook emission and a local file read, so a committed copy is a nonce published to anything that can read the repository, and the check it backs would then certify text that had merely read history.

paths.name: .beat-inflight
paths.reason: Sidecar marking a wait-for-deliverable beat as in flight. Exists only between a beat's start and its end.

paths.name: .context-sensor-state
paths.reason: Context sensor fire state, per pipeline. Tracked in the reference consumer, which is one of this release's three subjects; ai-dlc-recover.sh deletes it on recovery, so a committed copy resurrects a fire state the pipeline had deliberately cleared.

paths.name: .cycle-err
paths.reason: PID-suffixed error capture, written only on the fallback path taken when mktemp is unavailable. The glob is why this entry's ignore pattern differs from its name.

paths.name: .driver
paths.reason: Session-driver runtime markers -- handoff, idle, turns -- exchanged between the tmux launcher and the driver-signal hook. Tracked in the reference consumer, which is one of this release's three subjects.

paths.name: .recover-fired
paths.reason: One-shot marker that recovery has already run for this compaction. A committed copy suppresses recovery in a fresh clone.

paths.name: .recover-gate-progress
paths.reason: Progress marker for the recovery gate, read once and discarded.

paths.name: .wait-beats
paths.reason: Per-shell wait counters -- .shell-<pid>, <n>.since, <n>.progress -- created and destroyed constantly. 134 of them were tracked in the reference consumer and 5 of the 25 files in one handoff commit were this directory's churn. The finding that produced this whole declaration.

paths.name: handoff-guard-state.txt
paths.reason: Handoff guard state for the current session. One of the three transient names that is NOT dot-prefixed, which is why the partition is enumerated rather than derived from a dot-glob.

paths.name: pipeline-block-state.txt
paths.reason: Check 3 rapid-fire backoff counter, two lines, reset per run. Ignored in the reference consumer only by accident -- its .gitignore carries a blanket *.txt -- so the rule is stated here rather than left to a coincidence another consumer will not share.

paths.name: pipeline-paused.flag
paths.reason: Pause flag, deleted by the lead on resume. A tracked copy pauses every checkout.

paths.name: .handoff-in-progress
paths.reason: Handoff entry marker, written by the PostToolUse Read hook when the lead opens steps/handoff.md and removed by that file at step 5. Means the lead is INSIDE the handoff procedure, which is what ai-dlc-recover.sh routes a post-compact Read on. A tracked copy makes every checkout look mid-handoff.

paths.name: ai-dlc-update
paths.reason: Pull ledgers and the layer adjudication register. Committed evidence of what each pull decided.

paths.name: arm-log.jsonl
paths.reason: Append-only record of sensor arm firings, read across sessions.

paths.name: audit-anchors.md
paths.reason: The consumer's audit anchor declarations.

paths.name: compaction-log.md
paths.reason: One row per compaction. The corpus several retro measurements are taken over.

paths.name: context-mode-protection-log.md
paths.reason: Record of protected-path interceptions.

paths.name: gate-adjudication
paths.reason: Per-gate adjudication verdicts. Committed evidence a later gate reads.

paths.name: gate-metrics.jsonl
paths.reason: Gate timing and outcome metrics, accumulated across sprints.

paths.name: gate-log.md
paths.reason: The gate log itself. Archived, never regenerated.

paths.name: implementation-artifacts
paths.reason: Sprint implementation output -- gate log, metrics, sprint status.

paths.name: operator-answers-history.md
paths.reason: Verbatim AskUserQuestion answers. The evidence trail for a decision taken on the answer channel.

paths.name: operator-requests-history.md
paths.reason: Verbatim operator prose steers, the counterpart trail to the answers history.

paths.name: party-mode-transcripts
paths.reason: Retro transcripts a validator reads as retro evidence.

paths.name: pipeline-continuation-log.md
paths.reason: Every continuation event. The log this program's stall analysis was measured over.

paths.name: pipeline-snapshot-history.md
paths.reason: Rotated snapshot history, explicitly never deleted -- validate-snapshot-conservation.sh checks that lines only accumulate.

paths.name: pipeline-snapshot.md
paths.reason: The live pipeline position. Recovery reads it after a compaction, so it must survive a clone.

paths.name: pipeline-snapshot.precompact.md
paths.reason: The pre-compaction sidecar the recovery path diffs against. Durable because a compaction can be followed by a session that never saw the original.

paths.name: planning-artifacts
paths.reason: Stories, gate repairs, sprint status, carry-over backlog -- the largest committed tree under root.

paths.name: spawn-ledger.jsonl
paths.reason: One row per teammate spawn, read across sessions by the dispatch guard.

paths.name: subagent-context.jsonl
paths.reason: Subagent context probe output, accumulated as telemetry.

paths.name: validation-cycle-log.md
paths.reason: Validation cycle record, read by the cycle-commit audit.
